title: Percentages
description: Working out percentages of amounts, percentage increase and decrease, and expressing one quantity as a percentage of another.

notes.heading: What is a Percentage?
notes.body: Percentage means 'out of 100'. The symbol % stands for 'per cent', which means 'for every hundred'. So 50% means 50 out of 100, or one half. 100% means the whole amount, and 0% means none of it. Percentages can be written as fractions with denominator 100: 25% = 25/100 = 1/4.

notes.heading: Percentage of an Amount (Non-Calculator Methods)
notes.body: Break the percentage into easy pieces. To find 10% of an amount, divide by 10. To find 50%, divide by 2. To find 25%, divide by 4. To find 1%, divide by 100. Build other percentages from these. Example: find 30% of 80. 10% of 80 = 8, so 30% = 3 × 8 = 24. Example: find 15% of 60. 10% = 6 and 5% = 3, so 15% = 6 + 3 = 9.

notes.heading: Percentage Increase and Decrease
notes.body: To increase by a percentage, find the percentage of the amount and add it on. To decrease, find the percentage and subtract it. Example: increase 40 by 20%. 20% of 40 = 8, so new amount = 40 + 8 = 48. Example: decrease 90 by 10%. 10% of 90 = 9, so new amount = 90 − 9 = 81. Common mistake: do not just write the percentage; you must apply it to the original amount.

notes.heading: One Number as a Percentage of Another
notes.body: Write the first number as a fraction of the second, then multiply by 100. Formula: (part ÷ whole) × 100. Example: what is 12 out of 40 as a percentage? 12/40 = 0.3, then 0.3 × 100 = 30%. Make sure the denominator is the total amount you are comparing to, not the other way round. Example: if a test has 25 marks and you score 22, your percentage is 22/25 × 100 = 88%.

notes.heading: Real-World Percentages
notes.body: Percentages appear everywhere: discounts in shops, tax, tips, test scores, interest, and surveys. A 15% discount means you pay 85% of the original price. A 20% tip means you pay 120% of the meal cost. Always check whether the question asks for the amount saved or the final price, and read carefully.

flashcards.term: One number as a percentage of another
flashcards.definition: Divide the part by the whole and multiply by 100.

questions.explanation: Percentage means 'out of 100', so 50% means 50 out of 100, which is one half.
To find 10% of a number, divide by 10. 120 ÷ 10 = 12.
25% is the same as one quarter, so divide 80 by 4 to get 20.
10% of 50 is 5, so 30% is 3 times 5, which equals 15.

questions.stem: A jacket costs £80 and is reduced by 20%. How much is the discount?
questions.explanation: 20% of £80 is found by 80 ÷ 5 = £16, so the discount is £16.

questions.stem: What is the sale price of the £80 jacket after a 20% discount?
questions.explanation: The discount is £16, so subtract that from £80 to get the sale price of £64.
10% of 70 is 7, and adding this to 70 gives the increased value of 77.
25% of 120 is 30, so subtract 30 from 120 to get the decreased value of 90.

questions.stem: A student scores 18 out of 24 on a test. What is this as a percentage?
questions.explanation: Divide 18 by 24 to get 0.75, then multiply by 100 to change it to 75%.

questions.stem: What is 12 out of 40 as a percentage?
questions.explanation: 12 ÷ 40 = 0.3, and multiplying by 100 gives the percentage answer 30%.

questions.stem: A meal costs £40. A 10% tip is added. How much is paid in total?
questions.explanation: 10% of £40 is £4, so the total amount paid is £40 + £4 = £44.
10% of 300 is 30, so 5% is half of that, giving the final answer 15.
